headline: Oxa's new Dubai and port deployments mean the same rack of sensor logs gets driven again and again, so the bottleneck is choosing which of those near-identical frames to label in 3D and 2D, not labelling capacity itself.
what_they_build: Oxa sells a universal AI driver for industrial vehicles: self-driving software, modular up-fit hardware and fleet management for ports, airports, yards and factories. Buyers are logistics and infrastructure operators such as DHL (Heathrow), bp and Port of Tyne, plus the new SHIFFT joint venture with Dubai Future Foundation. Revenue comes from site deployments and fleet software, so perception quality per site is the product.
inferred_pipeline: Multi-camera plus LIDAR (and likely radar, GNSS/IMU) logged from up-fitted industrial vehicles running repetitive fixed routes at customer sites. Guess: ROS-style bags or a proprietary log format in cloud object storage.

Ingest into Oxa Foundry, their internal toolchain, with some multimodal search over clips, based on their October 2025 post 'Accelerating self-driving software development with multimodal search'. Guess: embedding search exists but curation is still engineer-driven.
Triage by scenario or trigger (disengagements, safety driver interventions, near misses) to pick clips for labelling. Guess.

Labelling split between 3D cuboids on point clouds and 2D boxes/masks on camera, likely via an external vendor or mixed internal/outsourced teams. Guess: 2D and 3D are not always labelled on the same synced clip.
Train and validate perception models, then site-specific validation and safety case evidence before deployment.
Redeploy to a new site (Dubai, a new port) and repeat much of the cycle because of domain shift. Guess, but strongly implied by the SHIFFT and Port of Tyne news.

hypotheses.pain: Repetitive fixed routes generate huge volumes of near-duplicate frames; teams pay to label redundancy and models plateau because rare edge cases are buried.
hypotheses.evidence: Site-based operation in ports, airports and yards on repeated routes, plus their own post on multimodal search to accelerate development.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Index registers data in their own bucket, computes embeddings and quality metrics per frame, and supports similarity search and diversity Collections. Our warehouse-robot test cut frames to label by 61% keeping 95% of racks, with higher mAP than a random pick of equal size.

hypotheses.pain: Each new site (Dubai, a new port) is a fresh domain: new vehicle types, ground markings, weather and lighting, so labelled data does not transfer and the cold start repeats.
hypotheses.evidence: SHIFFT joint venture with Dubai Future Foundation, Port of Tyne project and Heathrow via DHL, all announced within months of each other.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Active correlates data metrics with model failures to show which slices break at the new site, so you label only the gap. Agents can run an existing Oxa model as a pre-labelling stage so site two starts from predictions, not blank frames.

hypotheses.pain: Synced 3D point cloud and multi-camera labelling is handled in separate tools or vendor pipelines, so cross-modal consistency and QA cost engineering time.
hypotheses.evidence: Inferred from the sensor stack rather than stated. Their site mentions safety, validation and monitoring but nothing about annotation tooling. Flagging this as a guess.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Annotate supports 3D point clouds/LIDAR and native video in one ontology with object tracking and interpolation, plus annotate to review to complete workflows with sampled review. Active then finds label errors before they reach training.

ontology.name: Vehicle (tug, forklift, truck, dolly, GSE)
ontology.why: Primary dynamic obstacle in yards and airside; needs metric position for planning

ontology.name: Person / ground crew
ontology.why: Highest safety class; needs precise boundary at range and partial occlusion

ontology.name: Container, ULD, pallet or trailer
ontology.why: Static-but-movable load objects that define drivable space at a terminal

ontology.name: Drivable surface and restricted zone
ontology.why: Yards lack lanes; free space and keep-out areas drive path planning

ontology.name: Painted marking, kerb, stop line
ontology.why: Site-specific ground infrastructure that varies by port and airport

ontology.name: Dock, charger or trailer coupling point
ontology.why: Precise docking and hitching manoeuvres need a single anchor point

ontology.name: Scene condition (site, weather, lighting, surface)
ontology.why: Enables slicing model performance by site and condition in Active

ontology.name: Signal, sign or barrier state
ontology.why: Gate and barrier state changes behaviour; cheap to label as 2D box

case_study.name: Automotus
case_study.why_it_matches: Fixed-position cameras watching the same kerb over and over, which is the closest public analogue to Oxa's repeated fixed routes at a port or airside. The win came from curating the redundancy out, not from labelling faster.
case_study.numbers: +20% mAP, 35% smaller dataset, 33% lower labelling cost after curating with Encord.

proof_of_value: Week 1, day 1-2: register one site's logs (say Port of Tyne or a Heathrow yard) from Oxa's own S3/GCS via Index. No data movement, read-only credentials. Success: embeddings and quality metrics on 100k+ frames without a copy.

Week 1, day 3-5: build Collections by similarity and diversity across one month of repeated runs. Success: show what percentage of frames are near-duplicates and produce a curated pick that Oxa's perception lead agrees covers the route.

Week 2, day 1-2: label a synced 2D/3D slice in Annotate with Oxa's ontology, using SAM 3 and object tracking, plus one Agents stage running an existing Oxa detector as pre-labelling. Success: time per clip versus their current baseline.

Week 2, day 3-4: import Oxa predictions into Active and slice mAP/F1 by class, distance, weather and site. Success: name the three data slices that correlate with failure and the label errors found in the existing set.

Week 2, day 5: train or evaluate on curated versus random picks of equal size. Success metric agreed up front, for example equal or better mAP at 40% fewer labelled frames, plus a cost per site figure for the Dubai rollout.
discovery_questions: Your October 2025 post talked about multimodal search speeding up development. What does that cover today, and where does it stop being enough?
When you stand up a new site like Dubai, roughly how many labelled frames do you need before perception is signed off, and how much of that is genuinely new versus a repeat of Heathrow or Tyne?
Are 3D point cloud and camera labelled on the same synced clip today, and who does the 3D work, internal team or vendor?
How do you currently decide which clips from a week of repeated route runs actually get sent for labelling?
What does Oxa Foundry own that you would never outsource, and where would you rather buy than build?
risks: Oxa Foundry is an internal toolchain and they have already invested in multimodal search, so this is a build-versus-buy fight, not a greenfield one.
No open ML/CV job ads found and no contact identified, so we have no direct evidence of a hiring or tooling gap. The pain is inferred.
Fresh capital ($103m Series D first close, March 2026) and the SHIFFT launch means attention is on commercial rollout in Dubai, not on internal tooling procurement.
Likely NVIDIA ecosystem ties (their September 2025 note on NVIDIA technology expansion) could pull them toward an NVIDIA-aligned data stack instead.
Automotive-grade AV teams often have incumbent 3D labelling vendors on long contracts.
